candidates.current_role: U.S. Representative for Texas' 25th District since 2013
candidates.background: Roger Williams was raised in Fort Worth, attended Texas Christian University and played in the Atlanta Braves farm system. He runs a family-owned car dealership and cattle operation and coached baseball at TCU. He was first elected to Congress in 2012 and lives in Weatherford.

priorities.text: Prioritizes lower taxes and federal spending cuts.
Prioritizes deregulation and help for small businesses.
Prioritizes border security and support for Israel.

record.text: On the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), the 2025 budget reconciliation law that extended tax cuts and reduced projected federal Medicaid spending: voted yes on roll call 145; voted yes on roll call 190.
Did not vote on the Laken Riley Act (S. 5), which requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft-related or certain violent crimes, in January 2025.
Voted for the SAVE Act (H.R. 22), which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, in April 2025.
Voted for the Protect Children's Innocence Act (H.R. 3492), which would make certain gender transition procedures on minors a federal crime, in December 2025.
Voted for the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act (H.R. 498), which would bar Medicaid funding for gender transition procedures for minors, in December 2025.
Voted against H.J.Res. 72, a resolution to end the national emergency used to impose tariffs on Canadian goods, in February 2026.
Voted against H.R. 1834, which would extend expanded Affordable Care Act premium tax credits for three years and passed the House 230 to 196, in January 2026.
Voted for the Secure America Act (S. 2), which passed the House on a party-line vote, in June 2026.
Did not vote on the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (H.R. 21) in January 2025.
Introduced the Bulletproof Law Enforcement Vehicles Act to allow federal funds for police vehicle security upgrades.

q_voting_access.summary: Voted for the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

q_trans_minors.summary: Voted for a bill to make certain gender transition procedures on minors a federal crime and for a ban on Medicaid funding for such procedures for minors.

q_tariffs.summary: Voted against ending the national emergency used to impose tariffs on Canadian goods.

q_abortion.summary: Describes himself as pro-life.

q_gun_laws.summary: Describes himself as a Second Amendment supporter.
